cleanIntro: This is the Mafteah's own book and nothing in it belongs to another model, so every step below comes from the one document. Two things about this firearm change how you read it. It is recoil-operated rather than gas-operated, so the recoil spring rides on the magazine tube and comes out with the action bars rather than living in a stock you never open. And it has a birdshead grip instead of a buttstock, so there is no stock to rest against the bench while you pull the forend forward — you are holding the whole firearm by the grip and the barrel at the same time, which is the part people underestimate the first time.

steps.title: Empty, and empty again — the tube holds shells the chamber does not
steps.action: Run the unloading procedure through to the end before you touch the magazine cap. On a tube-fed semi-auto the chamber and the magazine are two separate reservoirs, so a chamber you have looked into tells you nothing about the four or five shells that may still be under the carrier. Lock the bolt back, look into the chamber, put a finger in it, then cycle the action until the tube stops feeding and nothing more comes out. IWI puts this warning at the head of the disassembly section rather than in a footnote, and the reason is that the next step you take releases spring tension at the front of the firearm.
steps.quote: Be sure the MAFTEAH Shotgun is unloaded before starting the disassembly! Keep the muzzle pointed in a safe direction.
steps.cite: MAFTEAH SHOTGUN OPERATOR MANUAL — V5.21.25 — read from the file name IWI publishes it under, IWI-Mafteah-Manual-V5.21.25.pdf — Section 10, Disassembly and Assembly, p.28
steps.warn: The tube can be loaded with the chamber empty. Cycle it dry before you start.

steps.title: Magazine cap off the front of the tube
steps.action: With the bolt closed, unscrew the magazine cap from the muzzle end of the magazine tube. It is hand-tight by design — the reassembly instruction says to seat it firmly by hand and nothing more — so it should come loose with finger pressure and no tool. If it will not turn, stop and check the tube is actually empty and the forend is not binding it, because a cap fought with a tool is a cap that will be over-torqued on the way back.
steps.quote: Unscrew the magazine cap located at the front of the magazine tube.
steps.cite: MAFTEAH SHOTGUN OPERATOR MANUAL — V5.21.25 — read from the file name IWI publishes it under, IWI-Mafteah-Manual-V5.21.25.pdf — Section 10.2, Disassembling the Receiver, p.29

steps.title: Hold the barrel down, slide the forend off forward
steps.action: Pull down on the vented rib to keep the barrel seated against the receiver, then draw the polymer forend forward off the magazine tube. The downward pressure is the whole trick: the barrel is only held by the bolt at this point, and letting it rise as the forend passes over it is what makes the forend feel jammed. Keep the muzzle pointed away and expect the forend to come free suddenly once it clears the tube.
steps.quote: Hold the barrel in place by pulling downward on the vented rib against the receiver, then separate the polymer forend by pulling forward and sliding it off.
steps.cite: MAFTEAH SHOTGUN OPERATOR MANUAL — V5.21.25 — read from the file name IWI publishes it under, IWI-Mafteah-Manual-V5.21.25.pdf — Section 10.2, Disassembling the Receiver, p.29

steps.title: Bolt carrier halfway back, then the barrel comes forward
steps.action: Draw the bolt carrier about halfway to the rear. That unlocks the bolt from the barrel extension and frees the barrel to come straight forward out of the receiver. Halfway is the position that matters — fully forward leaves the bolt locked into the extension and the barrel will not move, and fully rearward is past the point where the lugs clear. If the barrel resists, the carrier is in the wrong place, not the barrel.
steps.quote: Pull the bolt carrier halfway to the rear to unlock the bolt from the barrel extension and remove the barrel.
steps.cite: MAFTEAH SHOTGUN OPERATOR MANUAL — V5.21.25 — read from the file name IWI publishes it under, IWI-Mafteah-Manual-V5.21.25.pdf — Section 10.2, Disassembling the Receiver, p.29

steps.title: Charging handle straight out of the right side
steps.action: With the carrier still slightly to the rear, pull the charging handle out of the right side of the bolt carrier. It is a slip-fit and comes out sideways, not rearward. Note which way round it sits as it leaves — the reassembly instruction says the thicker portion faces forward, and a handle put back the other way will not seat fully, which is the most common reassembly fault on this firearm.
steps.quote: Pull the bolt carrier slightly to the rear and remove the charging handle by pulling it out of the right side of the bolt carrier.
steps.cite: MAFTEAH SHOTGUN OPERATOR MANUAL — V5.21.25 — read from the file name IWI publishes it under, IWI-Mafteah-Manual-V5.21.25.pdf — Section 10.2, Disassembling the Receiver, p.30

steps.title: Action bars, recoil spring and bolt group out the front
steps.action: Everything now leaves through the front of the receiver as one handful: the action bar assembly, the recoil spring that rides around the magazine tube, and the bolt group sitting on the rear of the bars. This is the part that surprises people coming from a gas gun — the spring is out here on the tube rather than buried in a stock, so it is exposed the moment the forend is off. Control it as it comes forward rather than letting it jump off the tube.
steps.quote: Remove the action bars, recoil spring and bolt group from the front of the receiver.
steps.cite: MAFTEAH SHOTGUN OPERATOR MANUAL — V5.21.25 — read from the file name IWI publishes it under, IWI-Mafteah-Manual-V5.21.25.pdf — Section 10.2, Disassembling the Receiver, p.30

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: You have the receiver, the barrel, the forend, the magazine cap, and the action bars with the recoil spring and bolt group. IWI states plainly that this is the point at which the firearm can be cleaned, and for routine maintenance it is where you stop. Everything the cleaning section asks for is reachable from here: the bore and chamber from the breech, the bolt face and under the extractor, the interior of the receiver, and the bolt rail.
steps.quote: The weapon is now field stripped and can be cleaned.
steps.cite: MAFTEAH SHOTGUN OPERATOR MANUAL — V5.21.25 — read from the file name IWI publishes it under, IWI-Mafteah-Manual-V5.21.25.pdf — Section 10.2, Disassembling the Receiver, p.30

deepSteps.title: Trigger group out — and no further
deepSteps.action: Push the trigger group retention pin through the receiver from left to right, then rotate the group downward from the rear and pull it forward. That gives you access to clean around it. It does not give you licence to open it: IWI states in the same numbered step that disassembling the trigger carrier group voids the warranty. Clean it as an assembly with degreaser and a brush, dry it, and put a light oil on it.
deepSteps.quote: The trigger group can now be accessed for additional cleaning: do not disassemble the trigger carrier group. This will void the warranty.
deepSteps.cite: MAFTEAH SHOTGUN OPERATOR MANUAL — V5.21.25 — read from the file name IWI publishes it under, IWI-Mafteah-Manual-V5.21.25.pdf — Section 10.2, Disassembling the Receiver, p.31
deepSteps.warn: Opening the trigger carrier group voids IWI's warranty. Clean it assembled.

deepSteps.title: The shell stop is a roll pin you should probably leave alone
deepSteps.action: The bolt release and shell stop assembly comes out by removing the T-20 torx screw and button head, then driving the shell stop roll pin from the bottom of the receiver toward the top with a 2mm roll pin punch. Before you do: IWI says in that same note that removing this assembly is not normally needed for maintenance, and that a roll pin which has been driven out should be replaced rather than reused, because a reused pin holds less well. Unless something is actually wrong with the shell stop, clean around it and leave the pin where it is.
deepSteps.quote: removal of this assembly is not normally needed or recommended for maintenance.
deepSteps.cite: MAFTEAH SHOTGUN OPERATOR MANUAL — V5.21.25 — read from the file name IWI publishes it under, IWI-Mafteah-Manual-V5.21.25.pdf — Section 10.2, Disassembling the Receiver, p.32
deepSteps.warn: A reused roll pin retains worse. Fit a new one if you drive the old one out.

deepSteps.title: Magazine tube: two tabs, and the tube pointed away from you
deepSteps.action: Point the magazine tube away from your face before anything else — there is a spring behind the cap. Depress the right and left tabs at the front of the tube cap with two small punches, press both inward together, and capture the cap as it releases. Then take out the cap, the magazine spring and the follower. Both tabs have to be in at once; working one at a time is what makes the cap let go unexpectedly.
deepSteps.quote: Using two small punches, depress the right and left tabs at the front of the magazine tub cap while pointing the tube away from you.
deepSteps.cite: MAFTEAH SHOTGUN OPERATOR MANUAL — V5.21.25 — read from the file name IWI publishes it under, IWI-Mafteah-Manual-V5.21.25.pdf — Section 10.2, Disassembling the Receiver, p.33
deepSteps.warn: Spring tension behind the cap. Tube away from your face, both tabs together.

deepSteps.title: Firing pin, cam pin, bolt — and that is the end of it
deepSteps.action: Drive the tapered pin at the rear top of the carrier downward and out with a 1/16 punch, then take out the firing pin and its spring. Lift the cam pin from the top of the carrier and pull the bolt forward out of the front. IWI ends the section there in capitals, and it is worth reading as written: the bolt itself is not meant to come apart further. Clean the firing pin channel by spraying a small amount of degreaser from the rear of the bolt toward the firing pin hole, and leave the bolt face clean and dry.
deepSteps.prose: The spelling is IWI's own; the sentence is quoted as printed.
deepSteps.quote: NO FURTHER DISASEMBLY OF THE BOLT IS REQUIRED
deepSteps.cite: MAFTEAH SHOTGUN OPERATOR MANUAL — V5.21.25 — read from the file name IWI publishes it under, IWI-Mafteah-Manual-V5.21.25.pdf — Section 10.2, Disassembling the Receiver, p.34

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Barrel out of the receiver, worked from the CHAMBER end toward the muzzle every time
Solvent-soaked patch on a rod and jag, pushed chamber to muzzle
12-gauge bronze bore brush, chamber to muzzle, then inspect the bore for remaining fouling
Wet patch with gun oil, then alternate dry and wet until the patch comes out relatively clean
One dry patch last, so only a light film of oil is left in the barrel
Check the threads and any choke fitted for wear, chipping, damage or rust

cleaning.name: BOLT GROUP
tasks: Wipe the outside of the bolt assembly and clean under the extractor with a toothbrush
Dry the parts, then a thin coat between the bolt body and the bolt head
Firing pin channel: a small amount of degreaser sprayed from the rear of the bolt toward the firing pin hole
Bolt face wiped off and left clean and dry — no oil here
Bolt rail cleaned and lightly oiled

cleaning.name: RECEIVER & SHELL STOP
tasks: Interior surfaces of the receiver cleaned with gun cleaner and a plain cloth
Body interior wiped with a rag and left dry
A light oil on the inside of the receiver and the shell stop

cleaning.name: TRIGGER GROUP
tasks: Cleaned as an assembly — never opened
Degreaser or a toothbrush to lift carbon and debris off the group
Left clean and dry, then lightly oiled
Two to four times a year on normal use, or any time it has met rain, snow, salt water or humidity

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE TUBE
tasks: Cap, spring and follower out before the tube is cleaned
Tube interior cleaned and the follower checked to move freely
Nothing heavy left in the tube — thick oil here collects grit

reassembly: Confirm the chamber and the magazine tube are empty and the bore is clear of patch material.
Bolt into the front of the carrier with the extractor facing right and the cam pin hole visible through the kidney-shaped slot.
Cam pin in with the line across its tip parallel to the carrier — that alignment is what lines up the firing pin hole.
Firing pin spring onto the firing pin, in through the rear of the carrier, then the retaining pin through the bottom capturing the spring.
Press the front of the bolt and the rear of the firing pin and confirm free movement before going further.
Follower into the tube, then the spring, then the cap pressed in until the tabs snap into place.
Trigger group rotated in against the grip and up to the pin hole, then the retaining pin in from right to left until flush both sides.
Recoil spring around the magazine tube, action bars on with the bars facing upward, bolt group aligned to the cutout on the bottom of the carrier.
Charging handle in from right to left with the thicker portion facing FORWARD, or it will not seat fully.
Bolt group back halfway, barrel in, then lower the bolt.
Barrel held all the way rearward, forend slid over the tube with downward tension.
Magazine cap screwed on under rearward pressure until it clicks — firmly hand tightened, no tool.
fncheck: With the chamber and the magazine tube empty and the muzzle pointed somewhere harmless: cycle the charging handle several times and confirm the bolt runs and locks without binding, and that the charging handle is fully seated with its thicker portion forward. Confirm the magazine cap is firmly hand tight and the forend has no fore-and-aft play on the tube. Press the bolt release and confirm the carrier runs forward. Drop the follower down the tube and confirm it moves freely and returns. IWI's own instruction is to finish with a function test before the firearm is considered assembled.
